notes: Stock Source engine (Source SDK Base 2013 Multiplayer) server; RCON is the Valve Source protocol on the game port, so there is no separate RCON port setting - only rcon_password in fof/cfg/server.cfg. Confirmed by two independent configs: the developer-posted server.cfg in the game's own Server Administration thread and the LinuxGSM Game-Server-Configs FoF server.cfg; both set only rcon_password, both exec banned_user.cfg and banned_ip.cfg, both call writeid/writeip, and neither contains any port directive. Commands are engine-level, not FoF-specific. kickid takes a userid OR uniqueid plus a free-text message ('Kick a player by userid or uniqueid, with a message' in the SDK 2013 HL2DM command list; totalcsgo documents the same argument order as 'kickid <User ID> <Message>'), while plain kick takes a NAME (SDK 2013 list: 'Kick a player by name'; TF2 wiki: 'kick <name>'), so the two are not interchangeable - Legion Hosting's FoF page documents 'rcon kick <userid>', which is wrong for this engine and would silently miss, so kickid is recorded instead. Valve's own Console_Command_List page is NOT evidence for that distinction and must not be cited for it: it has no kickid entry at all and describes kick as 'Kick a player by slot, userid or name' (GoldSrc-era wording); it is retained here only for banid, removeid and say. banid's first argument is minutes with 0 = permanent and it accepts a Steam ID (TF2 wiki: 'banid <minutes> <steamid>', '0 minutes is a permanent ban'; totalcsgo: 'banid <Minutes> <User ID>', 'use the value 0 to permanently ban'; Legion Hosting echoes the same order). Bans and unbans are in-memory only: run writeid after any banid or removeid, or the change is lost on restart - which is why the developer's server.cfg execs the banned_*.cfg files and calls writeid/writeip. It is commonly reported that banid does not disconnect an already-connected player, so a full ban is banid then kickid; that specific behaviour was NOT verified against any source opened here. IP bans use addip/removeip against banned_ip.cfg and are not modelled. The Steam ID printed by 'status' is STEAM_x:y:z on older Source builds and [U:1:n] on newer ones; playerId.pattern accepts both (the alternation is wrapped in a non-capturing group so a consumer that anchors it does not silently loosen the match) and playerParse.linePattern accepts both plus the optional second numeric column some builds print. SourceMod/Metamod are commonly installed on FoF servers and add sm_kick/sm_ban, but those are addons and are deliberately not recorded as the stock interface. Not verified against a live server.
